title: Why Your WordPress Site Feels Slow (and How to Fix It)
excerpt: Most slow WordPress sites share the same five problems. Here is how to find and fix them before they cost you customers.
content:
Speed is the first thing a visitor feels and the last thing most owners check. After building sites for different industries, the same causes keep showing up.

## 1. Oversized images
A 4 MB hero image is the most common culprit. Export at the size it is displayed, use WebP, and lazy-load everything below the fold.

## 2. Too many plugins
Every plugin adds requests and code. Audit yearly, delete what you do not use, and replace heavy plugins with lighter alternatives.

## 3. Cheap hosting
A good design cannot hide a slow server. Look for hosting with server-level caching and PHP 8+.

## 4. No caching layer
Page caching alone can cut load time in half. Pair it with a CDN for global visitors.

## 5. Heavy page builders used carelessly
Elementor is fine when sections are built with restraint. Avoid deep nesting and unnecessary animations.

**Quick win:** run your homepage through PageSpeed Insights, fix the top three opportunities, and re-test.

title: What Makes a Website Convert: 5 Design Rules I Follow
excerpt: A beautiful site that does not bring enquiries is just an expensive brochure. These are the rules I design around.
content:
A website should do more than look good. It should guide the visitor toward one clear action.

## One goal per page
Every page needs a single primary action: call, book, buy or message. Everything else supports it.

## Show proof early
Logos, results and real project screenshots build trust faster than paragraphs of claims.

## Make the next step obvious
A visible button above the fold and again at the end of the page removes guesswork.

## Design for mobile first
Most visitors arrive on a phone. If the layout works there, desktop is the easy part.

## Keep it fast
Every extra second of load time loses visitors. Performance is part of design.
